name: When a fraction terminates
formula: \frac{a}{b} \text{ in lowest terms terminates} \iff b = 2^m 5^n\ (m, n \ge 0), \text{ with } \max(m, n) \text{ digits after the point}
whenToUse: Decide which fractions have terminating decimals, or how many digits a terminating decimal has after the point.
example: Among $\frac{1}{1}, \frac{1}{2}, \ldots, \frac{1}{20}$ the terminating ones have denominators $1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 16, 20$: eight of them. And $\frac{3}{40} = 0.075$ has $3$ digits, since $40 = 2^3 \cdot 5$.
pitfall: Reduce the fraction FIRST: $\frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}$ terminates even though $12$ has a factor of $3$.
